rendered: Water has the strongest hydrogen bonding of the solvents compared in the paper. The figure plotting hydrogen bonding strength for PVDF and the solvents (Figure 6b[1]) gives water's strength (δH) as δH value of 42.3 MPa^1/2[2]. For comparison, EG's δH is 26.0[3] in the same units (the Hansen solubility parameter table). Water is not used for delamination because it corrodes the aluminum foil: the document says it is suitable for delamination because the aluminum foil exhibited[4] corrosion from lithium leaching out of the NMC cathode, which making the water solution basic[5]. The corrosion then contaminates the cathode, since aluminum would form (OH)3 precipitates on the cathode surfaces[6]. EG was chosen instead because its high δH lets it form strong hydrogen bonds with the aluminum oxide layer and compete with PVDF for binding, while avoiding this corrosion problem.
